label: pjm 51 seam se
definition: (DIAGNOSTIC) pjm-49/50 seam base (pjm-48 coal keeper + MISO/NYISO hr_by_year + firm-export floor + losses hurdle + TVA/LGEE) + the one new lever: Southeast (Carolinas/TVA/LGEE) gas-INELASTIC affine reference price (_HR_GAS_ELASTIC 5.6*gas+14.2, OLS-fit to documented Into-Southern/SERC hub levels, BLIND to flow; derive_southeast_inelastic_hr.py). RESULT -- the named root cause is FIXED: the 2025 wrong-direction Southeast export flips back to correct IMPORT (Carolinas/TVA/LGEE per-seam +2.0/+1.3/+0.9 wrong at pjm-50 -> -4.4/-3.3/-2.5 vs per-tie -5.9/-5.4/-2.3). Old flat HR 11.6 priced SE at $40.8 in dear-gas 2025 (~$2 below PJM, diurnal swing flipped it export); the affine holds it at $33.9 (~$9 below PJM), so the structural import direction holds across the gas cycle. BUT the fix UNMASKS the dominant remaining error and UNIFIES it with the coal/gas class miss: correctly importing cheap SE power lowers PJM's modeled price, so PJM out-competes MISO/NYISO and over-exports MORE (2025 MISO +37.8 vs pjm-50 +20.0; net-interchange MAE vs EIA-930 rises to 23.5 from pjm-50's 15.2). The flat-SE was MASKING this by bleeding excess off as spurious SE exports. The MISO/NYISO seams already carry convex self-limiting (load_shape_exponent 1.6) yet still saturate at the cap -- because the over-export is NOT a seam-pricing bug but PJM being structurally UNDER-priced: it over-generates fossil (gas +73 TWh 2025, coal classes off) which makes it cheaper than its neighbors. So 'import/export' and 'class missed' are the SAME root cause -- PJM's fleet is too cheap. The SE gas-inelastic pricing is structurally correct and stays in (rule #1) even though net worsens; pjm-48 remains the PJM keeper. Next: the coal/gas offer-curve retune (the keeper's separate model-side workstream) is the lever for BOTH; a Southeast FIRM-IMPORT floor (mirror of the firm-export floor) recovers the 2024 SE import the affine price correctly stops faking. Years 2023-25, single-process sequential solve.
